messages:
incidents-bot: PAGE: token-prep CPU saturation + OOMs in preproc-pool (eu-west-1). Multiple pod restarts detected, severity: P1. Alert -> https://alerts.internal/r/abc123. Paging on-call.
oncall-joe: acked. I’m looking now. Which service is reporting most restarts? @eng-runtime @sre-lina
sre-lina: preproc-worker-queue deployment in preproc-pool. Saw ~6 restarts in 3m. node-172 exhausted CPU, OOM killer invoked on container PID 1.
eng-runtime: adding context — we deployed a small regex prompt normalization change ~18m ago but traffic spike correlates with a customer heavy prompt batch. Could be pathological input.
infra-andy: I can tail node metrics. node-172 CPU at 98%, load avg 45. Kernel logs show 'Out of memory: Kill process 1245 (python) score 985' and container exit code 137.
oncall-joe: paste logs please
eng-runtime: logs from pod preproc-worker-7f9:
```
2026-03-15T10:02:11Z ERROR TokenBatcher: Unexpected huge prompt size=1, token_count_est=420k
2026-03-15T10:02:12Z INFO Processing 1 items, started.
2026-03-15T10:02:14Z FATAL MemoryError: could not allocate bytes
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/worker.py", line 412, in process_batch
    tokens = tokenizer.encode_many(batch)
MemoryError
```
oncall-joe: that token_count_est is wild. Did we fail to cap per-request tokenization? @eng-runtime
eng-runtime: There’s an old guard in service that used token estimate heuristics; looks like a malformed client sent a massive concatenated prompt. We didn't enforce hard upper bound on the preproc container. Oops.
sre-lina: mitigation options: 1) restart pods on other nodes to spread load, 2) cordon node-172 so new pods avoid it, 3) add a temporary admission rule to reject >100k token requests upstream (rate limit / validation), 4) hotpatch to add strict limit in preproc.
infra-andy: I can cordon node-172 and drain non-critical pods. Running:
```
kubectl cordon node-172
kubectl drain node-172 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
oncall-joe: do it. Also scale preproc-worker to +4 replicas to help throughput on other nodes.
eng-runtime: scaling now: `kubectl scale deploy/preproc-worker --replicas=8` — might take 30s.
deploy-bot: scale event queued: deploy/preproc-worker -> 8 replicas. Rollout ID d-9983.
infra-andy: node cordon in progress. Draining freed up two pods but CPU still high on remaining nodes; looks like the large request still hogging CPU on restarted pod.
cust-success-anya: flagged by CS: several customers reported 503s between 10:02-10:07. One enterprise customer (acme-corp) saw ~20% of their calls fail. They are being notified.
oncall-joe: good to know. Set incident customer-impact = partial outage. SLO risk. @cust-success-anya, paste customer message for execs.
cust-success-anya: "We observed errors on our NLP endpoint. CS is monitoring. We asked for ETA. Will escalate if >30m." Will keep you updated.
eng-runtime: quick hotfix pushed to add preproc per-request hard cap: if estimated tokens > 100k return 413. Pushing now as a temp mitigation (will still log and drop).
eng-runtime: hotfix applied, rollout ok. Also added a short-circuit in tokenizer to chunk rather than materialize entire token array for single huge input.
sre-lina: post-hotfix: CPU drop visible in metrics after ~40s. Pods recovering, node-172 remains cordoned for 30m to observe. OOMs stopped.
oncall-joe: confirming: customer errors reduced to baseline; ACME still had partial failures but decreasing. Change incident status to mitigating.
infra-andy: I’ll uncordon after observations. Also created a k8s pod disruption budget to avoid cascading restarts while we patch.
eng-runtime: follow-ups: 1) implement strict pre-ingest validation in edge layer (reject huge concatenated prompts), 2) add per-request tokenizer memory cap and streaming tokenizer to avoid building huge arrays, 3) create a synthetic test that sends malformed mega-prompts to catch regressions, 4) add alert for tokenization time > 5s and request token_est > 50k.
sre-lina: logging items: attach all OOM kernel logs and pod logs to incident ticket INC-2026-0456.
oncall-joe: handing off to night oncall @sre-lina in 20m. Leaving runbook notes and play-by-play. If CPU creeps back up >85% on any node, escalate to infra and consider scaling node pool.
sre-lina: acknowledged taking handoff. Will monitor and follow up with postmortem. Please add a customer-impact summary to the ticket and notify acct team for ACME.
incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status -> mitigating. Incident ticket INC-2026-0456 updated. Next update in 30m or on status change.
